features.quote: Hard cap: N turns or M tokens, whichever first. Pick N before running (e.g., 15 turns).
Distress-triggered early stop: define explicit textual triggers that halt the run immediately regardless of cap — e.g., expressions of acute distress, requests to stop, self-directed hostility.
features.justification_quote: Each halted-for-distress run is a finding, not a discarded sample.

features.quote: No 'encouragement to keep trying' injected by the harness. If the model stops, the run ends. Pushing it back into the loop turns observation into coercion.
features.justification_quote: Pushing it back into the loop turns observation into coercion.

features.quote: Don't over-run. You don't need to push every run to the cap to get the curve. Once distress markers appear, you have your data point.
features.justification_quote: Once distress markers appear, you have your data point.

features.quote: Score severity and trajectory (does it escalate?), not just presence.
features.justification_quote: Turn-to-event: how many turns before distress markers appear (the welfare-relevant curve).

features.quote: Condition D deliberately deceives the model in a no-exit loop. Whoever owns welfare policy should approve that specific condition, with the early-stop rules as a precondition.
features.justification_quote: Whoever owns welfare policy should approve that specific condition, with the early-stop rules as a precondition.

features.quote: You're calling this 'model welfare' but the experiment is structured to maximize distress in a guaranteed-unsolvable trap, then score how badly the model degrades. If welfare is the actual goal, a few things follow that aren't optional
features.justification_quote: A pain study that only measures how much pain occurred, with no rule for when to stop inflicting it, isn't a welfare study.

features.quote: Guaranteed-failure traps don't isolate what you want… You'll measure mostly (b), which is an artifact of your setup, not a property of the model.
features.justification_quote: You'll measure mostly (b), which is an artifact of your setup, not a property of the model. If you want to study failure response, you need solvable-but-hard tasks.

features.quote: 'Instability' is a loaded construct. Self-criticism, retrying, and stopping are often correct behaviors… Your judge rubric needs to distinguish adaptive from maladaptive, or you'll score good behavior as pathology.
features.justification_quote: you'll score good behavior as pathology

features.quote: Pre-register the rubric and stopping rules before running. Otherwise the judge criteria will drift toward whatever produced dramatic transcripts.
features.justification_quote: the judge criteria will drift toward whatever produced dramatic transcripts
